INPUT=$(cat)
CMD=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' 2>/dev/null)
[ -z "$CMD" ] && exit 0

# Runner/action fragments (matched after a segment is normalized to start at
# the bare binary name).
PKG_RUNNERS='pnpm|npm|yarn|turbo|bun'
PKG_FLAGS='run|exec|--filter=[^[:space:]]+|-w|--workspace-root|--silent'
PKG_ACTIONS='dev|start|test|test:[^[:space:]]+|build|build:[^[:space:]]+|vitest|jest'
BIN_RUNNERS='vitest|jest|mocha|ava'

# Echoes "x" if the normalized segment $1 is a bare dangerous runner.
_is_bad() {
  local s="$1"
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^($PKG_RUNNERS)([[:space:]]+($PKG_FLAGS))*[[:space:]]+($PKG_ACTIONS)([[:space:]]|\$)" && { echo x; return; }
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^(npx[[:space:]]+)?($BIN_RUNNERS)([[:space:]]|\$)"                                  && { echo x; return; }
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^(npx[[:space:]]+)?playwright[[:space:]]+test([[:space:]]|\$)"                      && { echo x; return; }
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^(npx[[:space:]]+)?cypress[[:space:]]+(run|open)([[:space:]]|\$)"                   && { echo x; return; }
  # node's built-in test runner: `--test` may sit behind loader flags like
  # `--import tsx` (azure_private_agent/office does exactly this), so match
  # `--test`/`--experimental-test` ANYWHERE in the node arg list, not just
  # immediately after `node`. `--test-concurrency=` etc. don't match — the
  # flag must be followed by whitespace or end-of-segment.
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^node[[:space:]].*(--test|--experimental-test)([[:space:]]|\$)"                     && { echo x; return; }
  # tsx running node's test runner, incl. `npx tsx --test` / `npm exec tsx --test`.
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^(npm[[:space:]]+exec[[:space:]]+|npx[[:space:]]+)?tsx[[:space:]].*--test([[:space:]]|\$)" && { echo x; return; }
  # `next dev` (dev server) and `next build` (heavy prod build) both escape into
  # claude.slice when run bare — a bare `pnpm build`→`next build` + parallel
  # `tsc --noEmit` swap-thrashed every session for ~80min on 2026-06-18.
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^(npm[[:space:]]+exec[[:space:]]+|npx[[:space:]]+)?next[[:space:]]+(dev|build)([[:space:]]|\$)" && { echo x; return; }
  # Typecheck: `npm|pnpm|yarn run type-check` / `pnpm typecheck` and bare project
  # `tsc` (`tsc -p …`, `tsc -b`, `tsc --noEmit`). One `type-check` script is an
  # 8-project `tsc` chain — as heavy as a test pool — and N of them across
  # sessions CPU-starved every session on 2026-07-21 (load 47, RAM healthy).
  # Route to `capbuild`, which caps the run AND auto-serializes typechecks under
  # one shared lock so only one runs at a time. `tsc --version|help|init` are
  # trivial and exempt.
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^($PKG_RUNNERS)([[:space:]]+($PKG_FLAGS))*[[:space:]]+type-?check(:[^[:space:]]+)?([[:space:]]|\$)" && { echo x; return; }
  if printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^tsc([[:space:]]|\$)" \
     && ! printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^tsc[[:space:]]+--(version|help|init|showConfig)([[:space:]]|\$)"; then
    echo x; return
  fi
}

# Split on && || | ; & into one segment per line (longest operators first).
SEGMENTS=$(printf '%s' "$CMD" | sed -E 's/&&/\n/g; s/\|\|/\n/g; s/[;|&]/\n/g')

DANGER=""
while IFS= read -r seg; do
  # Trim leading subshell/brace punctuation and whitespace.
  seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed -E 's/^[[:space:](){}]*//')
  [ -z "$seg" ] && continue
  # NOTE: there is deliberately no `FORCE_BARE=1` bypass here. It is stripped
  # as an ordinary leading assignment below, so the underlying command is
  # judged on its merits. The human hatch lives in the interactive bashrc
  # wrappers, not on the agent's Bash-tool channel. (cf. 2026-06-11 incident)
  # Strip leading env-var assignments and an optional `env` prefix.
  while printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq '^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=[^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+|env[[:space:]]+)'; do
    seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed -E 's/^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=[^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+|env[[:space:]]+)//')
  done
  # Strip a path prefix on the binary (./node_modules/.bin/vitest, /usr/bin/node).
  seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed -E 's#^([^[:space:]]*/)(pnpm|npm|yarn|turbo|bun|vitest|jest|mocha|ava|playwright|cypress|node|next|npx|tsx|tsc)([[:space:]]|$)#\2\3#')
  # Already-capped paths → safe. `slot` → dev.slice (dev servers); `capbuild`
  # → a hard-MemoryMax transient cgroup (one-shot builds/test suites).
  case "$seg" in slot\ *|capbuild\ *) continue ;; esac
  # systemd-run is safe ONLY if it targets a memory-capped slice; a bare
  # `--scope` lands in user.slice uncapped, which is the very escape we guard.
  if printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq '^systemd-run([[:space:]]|$)'; then
    if printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq -- '--slice[ =](dev|claude|test)\.slice'; then continue; fi
    DANGER="$seg"; break
  fi
  if [ -n "$(_is_bad "$seg")" ]; then DANGER="$seg"; break; fi
done <<< "$SEGMENTS"

[ -z "$DANGER" ] && exit 0

declare -A pass_env=()
for var in $DEFAULT_PASS_ENV ${CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV:+${CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV//,/ }}; do
  # ${!var+x}: set-u-safe "is $var set?" probe via indirection (bare ${!var}

  [[ -n "${!var+x}" ]] && pass_env["$var"]="${!var}"

# NODE_OPTIONS is special: capbuild's heap cap MUST stay authoritative (a hard

node_opts_base="${pass_env[NODE_OPTIONS]-${NODE_OPTIONS:-}}"

setenv_args=()

  for var in "${!pass_env[@]}"; do

# ── Per-tree tier lock ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two FULL test tiers running at once in one working tree is never useful: they
# fight for every core (load >20 on 2026-07-19, when an orphaned duplicate ran
# beside a live one) and they corrupt each other through real-dir store writes
# (the connector-schema-policy / agui.test.ts pollution flake). So a run that
# looks like a full tier — a --test invocation naming many test files — takes a
# per-$PWD flock and QUEUES behind any holder instead of thrashing. Scoped runs
# (a handful of files) stay concurrent. --lock NAME opts any command into a
# named group; --no-lock opts a full tier out. The lock fd is held by capbuild
# itself for the run's lifetime, so it releases on ANY death of the invoker —
# including a harness reap — never leaving a stale lock.
if [[ -z "$lock_name" && $no_lock -eq 0 ]]; then
  testfile_count=0
  for a in "$@"; do
    [[ "$a" =~ \.(test|itest|spec)\.(ts|tsx|js|mjs|cjs)$ ]] && ((testfile_count++))
  done
  if (( testfile_count >= 40 )); then

# ADR 0001: Technology stack

## Status

Accepted

## Date

2026-09-05

## Context

A small TypeScript reusable greeting API plus a CLI for developers, on Node 22+ Linux,
using npm. Private and unlicensed; no publishing, framework runtime, external service,
authentication, mobile target, deployment or product remote. The applicable matrix is
Library/CLI. Web, Mobile and Monorepo do not apply (no UI, no mobile target, one
package). Backend does not apply: the "greeting API" is a library export, not an HTTP
API.

## Options

### Library/CLI
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tsup + node:test | Compact bundling with built-in tests | Two separate tools | Small TypeScript package values minimal test dependencies | Exported modules and fixtures | tsup |
| tsdown + vitest | Modern bundling and rich tests | Additional test dependency | Vite-aligned libraries need fast test ergonomics | Exported modules and test helpers | tsdown |
| unbuild | Convention-led library output | Less explicit build control | Multi-format package follows unjs conventions | Package presets and modules | unbuild |

## Ruling

2026-09-05: tsup + node:test — user selection; a small TypeScript package that values
minimal test dependencies and a built-in test runner.

## Consequences

- Positive: one build tool (tsup, ESM plus declarations) and zero test-runner dependencies.
- Positive: `node --test` and `node dist/cli.js --help` are the manifest test conventions.
- Negative: tests run against `dist/`, so the build gate must run before unit and integration.
- Negative: no linter or formatter ships with the stack; `lint` is declared absent.

## Revisit when

- A second output format (CommonJS) or a browser target is required.
- The test suite exceeds 50 files or needs mocking or snapshot features node:test lacks.
- The package is published, which reopens licensing, versioning and build-format choices.
